body:
I don't know if I can find the bandwidth to test, but these are my questions/investigations.

1. Does parallel betsy compiling work approximately the same as the old system in results?
2. Is it faster?
3. Is the code more complicated?
4. Since this code is load-bearing, I want to ensure it doesn't break anything since it's essential in the 3d import.

Other than that, the Betsy parallel compression looks good, and I want to get it in for testing, or we'll have to wait 6 months to a year for the next branch.
Imo it would be good to also get @clayjohn 's opinion on this, if possible

> I don't know if I can find the bandwidth to test, but these are my questions/investigations.
> 
>     1. Does parallel betsy compiling work approximately the same as the old system in results?
> 
>     2. Is it faster?
> 
>     3. Is the code more complicated?
> 
>     4. Since this code is load-bearing, I want to ensure it doesn't break anything since it's essential in the 3d import.

1. Yes, now the mipmaps are simply compressed at the same time, and after they're all done, they get copied from the GPU. Previously, each mipmap had to be compressed, then copied, one after another.

2. In 95% of cases they should be, since now the GPU is utilized more. On some systems with a GPU bottleneck it could be a bit slower, but I couldn't confirm it.

3. Kind of? In a way, it's simpler now, since previously it was kind of a mess with how the temporary textures were managed. 

4. I tested it on a few somewhat big projects, and it looks like it works as intended

Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/abf8e1e6f9e165ea209350ab9a98f01feca93b90), it works as expected.

However, I can't reproduce a performance improvement when importing large textures (a [4K PBR material](https://polyhaven.com/a/square_tiles_03) and a [8K4K HDRI](https://polyhaven.com/a/goegap_road), both with VRAM compression enabled). All textures have mipmap generation enabled.

## Benchmark

<details open>

<summary>PC specifications</summary>

- **CPU:** Intel Core i9-13900K
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
- **RAM:** 64 GB (2×32 GB DDR5-5800 C30)
- **SSD:** Solidigm P44 Pro 2 TB
- **OS:** Linux (Fedora 41)
</details>

File names with `hq` in them use the High Quality compresion option, which doesn't use Betsy for BPTC SDR. Betsy is used for BPTC HDR though. Either way, enabling High Quality has no effect on VRAM-compressed HDRIs, at least on desktop – they'll always use BPTC HDR.
